newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss Re net jumps 33 pct to 1.46 bln Sfr.
newsitem.headline: Swiss Re net jumps 33 pct to 1.46 bln Sfr.

text.p: Swiss Re said Friday that 1996 net profit jumped 33 percent to 1.46 billion Swiss francs ($993 million), overshooting even optimistic forecasts for the world's second biggest reinsurer and the leader in life and health reinsurance.
"The 1996 business year was once again very satisfying for the Swiss Re group," the company said in a statement released after the Swiss stock exchange closed for the weekend.

Analysts cheered the news. "The profit is great. Capital has also developed excellently and that's the number I look at, because it influences future profits through investment," said analyst Heinrich-Horst Wiemer at CS First Boston.
Swiss Re registered shares closed earlier 40 Swiss francs ($21.21) higher at 1,746 ($1188) in what traders called anticipation of a good financial scorecard.
Return on equity (ROE) was 13.8 percent after 12.7 percent in 1995, moving closer to a goal of 15 percent.
Swiss Re said its board of directors proposed raising the dividend to 30 francs from 22.50 on the basis of the 1996 gains and a "favorable assessment of current business trends."
It did not say anything more about the outlook for the current year, for which analysts have so far projected net profit between 1.45 billion ($986 million) and 1.6 billion $1.09 billion).

Net profit after minority interests was 1.459 billion ($993 million) or 100 Swiss francs ($68) per share, well above widespread estimates of growth rates between 20 percent and 28 percent from a 1995 net of 1.10 billion ($748 million) or 75 francs ($51) per share.
"This increase is due mainly to continued improvement in technical results and a much higher return on investment activities," Swiss Re said.
